cases.learnTitle: Cardiac MRI: the left atrium behind the aortic root
cases.contextSource: Dataset description (whole-heart MRI of adults at a university hospital); no clinical history, age or sex is distributed.
cases.referenceSummary: The left atrium is outlined by the dataset (King's College London, Medical Segmentation Decathlon): an expert segmented the left atrium, its appendage, the mitral plane and the pulmonary vein end points with an automated tool and then corrected the result by hand. It is semi-automatic and expert-corrected, not drawn from scratch, and has not been re-reviewed here. The dataset's outline contains the blood pool of the atrium with its appendage and the stumps of the pulmonary veins; the atrial wall is not separated and the mitral valve plane is the lower border. The other chambers and vessels are not outlined. Scanner: 1.5 T, free breathing with ECG and respiratory gating, one cardiac phase; images acquired at 1.25 mm and shown as axial slices every 2.5 mm.
cases.learnNotes: The left atrium is the most posterior chamber of the heart. On an axial slice at the level of the aortic root it lies in the middle, directly behind the aortic root and in front of the descending aorta, the esophagus and the spine. Pulmonary veins enter it at its back corners: the two right veins pass behind the right atrium, the two left veins run in front of the descending aorta. The left atrial appendage is a small ear-shaped pouch that curves forward beside the pulmonary trunk on the left, and the mitral valve opens from the lower front of the atrium into the left ventricle. On this 3D whole-heart MRI the blood is bright, the heart muscle grey and the lungs dark, so scroll from the aortic root down to the four-chamber level and follow the bright pool behind the aorta (Learning Radiology, Ch. 3).
